Time-series learning

EN-Beats

An ensemble learning method for multiple-resource prediction in cloud computing environments.

IEEE CLOUD · 2023·Published
Read paperAuthor PDF
On this pageThe problemMy contributionDesign decisionsEvaluationLimitationsPaper & resources

The problem

Cloud resource demand changes over time, and different resource signals can exhibit different patterns. Resource management benefits from anticipating demand before making scaling or placement decisions.

My contribution

I developed an ensemble learning approach for predicting multiple cloud resource demands, connecting time-series modeling with the needs of resource management.

Design decisions

Forecast across resource signals

Study multiple resource demands so that a prediction workflow can support decisions beyond a single utilization series.

Use ensemble learning

Combine predictive modeling choices to address variation in resource behavior across the evaluated datasets.

Connect prediction to system decisions

Treat forecasts as inputs to resource management, where evaluation must account for both prediction quality and the downstream use of the estimate.

Evaluation & outcomes

The IEEE CLOUD 2023 evaluation uses Bitbrains resource traces and a ten-minute forecasting horizon. Reported CPU NRMSE is 4.4%, compared with 5.84% for N-BEATS; memory NRMSE is 5.93%, compared with 8.22%. Results vary by resource and metric.

10 minforecasting horizon in the evaluated resource traces

What the results depend on

Forecasting quality is sensitive to the workload, prediction horizon, available history, and shifts in behavior. A deployment should validate the model against its own resource traces.
